findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), this yields 3 pages when only 2 exist. Because showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages, the 'next' button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset = min(offset + limit, user_count) = 100, and findMembers then fetches an empty page, leaving the admin looking at a blank 'page 3/3' of members with no way forward. The computation should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the zero case handled), and/or the next action should clamp offset to user_count - limit.

findings.title: 'automatic' check resolves against the member, so the remove button always renders
findings.body: This template is rendered as the itemView for each member in '{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}', so its context is the individual user, not the group. '{{#unless automatic}}' therefore looks up 'automatic' on a User, which is undefined, so the condition always passes and the remove (×) link is shown even for automatic groups (admins, moderators, etc.). Clicking it fires the DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members request, which the server correctly rejects with 422 (can_not_modify_automatic), but the client-side removeMember action in the admin-group controller and the Group model's removeMember have no error handling, so the click fails silently and the member just stays in the list. The automatic check needs to come from the group/controller (e.g. passed via the each or referenced through the controller), and the failure case should surface an error to the admin.

findings.title: Group create silently ignores the alias_level chosen in the form
findings.body: The client sends alias_level on creation: Discourse.Group.asJSON() returns {name, alias_level, visible} and create() POSTs it to /admin/groups, and the alias level combo box in admin/templates/group.hbs is shown for new (unsaved) groups too. However the create action only assigns name and visible — params[:alias_level] is never applied — so every new group is created with the default alias_level of 0 ('nobody') regardless of what the admin selected, with no feedback. The admin must save the group and then save it again via update (which does handle alias_level) to get the intended setting.

findings.title: Public group members page now truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: The members action now always applies limit/offset (default limit 50) to every group; previously non-automatic groups returned their full member list and only automatic groups were capped. The public-facing group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) was updated to read 'members' off the group model but has no pagination or load-more controls — only the admin group page got next/previous. As a result, any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 (alphabetically) on its public members page, with no way for a visitor to see the rest.

findings.title: members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit parameter
findings.body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i places no upper bound on the page size for this publicly accessible endpoint (anyone who can see the group can call it). A request such as /groups/mods/members.json?limit=1000000 forces a COUNT plus a full SELECT and JSON serialization of that many users in one request. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum (e.g. 200).

findings.title: remove_member 'automatic group' test uses PUT while the route is DELETE-only
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42, but the route added in config/routes.rb is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" — PUT /admin/groups/:id/members is not routed (PUT maps to add_members). Rails controller tests bypass the router and dispatch directly to the action, so this test passes anyway, which means it would not catch a missing or misconfigured DELETE route. It should use xhr :delete like the companion test does.
